title: Easy algebraization of a formal coherent module up to ideal-power torsion
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let I be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on X, let G be a coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let (F_n) be an object of Coh(X,I) [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. (1) If alpha:(F_n) -> G^ is a morphism whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of I [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-annihilated-by-power], then there are a coherent O_X-module F, a map a:F -> G whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of I, and an isomorphism beta:(F_n) -> F^ such that alpha = a^ beta; the triple is unique up to unique isomorphism. (2) If instead alpha:G^ -> (F_n) has kernel and cokernel annihilated by a power of I, then there are a coherent O_X-module F, a map a:G -> F whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of I, and an isomorphism beta:F^ -> (F_n) such that alpha = beta a^; this triple is unique up to unique isomorphism. (An isomorphism of triples $(\mathcal F,a,\beta)\to(\mathcal F',a',\beta')$ is an isomorphism $\gamma:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $a'\gamma=a$ and $\gamma^\wedge\beta=\beta'$ in case (1), resp. $\gamma a=a'$ and $\beta'\gamma^\wedge=\beta$ in case (2); 'unique up to unique isomorphism' means that between any two such triples there is exactly one isomorphism of triples.)

proof.text: For part (1), use [lem-weil-pbc-easy-algebraization-torsion-triple], the already stated source-faithful torsion-controlled version. Reorder the two conjuncts and the comparison hypotheses to match the present interface. This is a direct application of an existing declaration.

For part (2), use [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence-easy-from-exists] to obtain H, a, beta and the ordinary torsion bound. Given another torsion-controlled triple, set theta to beta followed by beta' inverse and theta' to beta' followed by beta inverse. The factorization equations imply that both formal maps commute with the completed maps from G.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-completion-isogeny-from-hom-lift] to lift theta to f and theta' to g. Apply its uniqueness to each identity formal map: f followed by g and the identity are lifts of the same map under G, so are equal; similarly g followed by f is the identity. Thus f and g define an isomorphism. Its equations follow from the lifting equations and beta inverse identities. For any second isomorphism of triples, cancel beta' to identify its completed hom with theta. Unique Hom lifting gives equality of homs, and Iso.ext gives equality of isomorphisms. All these steps are proved in Lean, with no hole in the parent module.

theorem grothendieckExistenceEasy (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (G : CoherentModules X)
    (F : CoherentFormalModule X I) :
    (∀ (α : F ⟶ (completion X I).obj G),
      (∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,
        IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
          (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2
          (kernel (α.hom.app (op n)))) ∧
        IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
          (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2
          (cokernel (α.hom.app (op n))))) →
      ∃ (H : CoherentModules X) (a : H ⟶ G)
        (β : F ≅ (completion X I).obj H),
        (∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧
          IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
            (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (kernel a.hom)) ∧
          IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
            (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (cokernel a.hom))) ∧
        α = β.hom ≫ (completion X I).map a ∧
        ∀ (H' : CoherentModules X) (a' : H' ⟶ G)
          (β' : F ≅ (completion X I).obj H'),
          (∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧
            IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
              (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (kernel a'.hom)) ∧
            IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
              (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (cokernel a'.hom))) →
          α = β'.hom ≫ (completion X I).map a' →
          ∃! γ : H ≅ H',
            γ.hom ≫ a' = a ∧
              β.hom ≫ (completion X I).map γ.hom = β'.hom) ∧
    (∀ (α : (completion X I).obj G ⟶ F),
      (∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,
        IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
          (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2
          (kernel (α.hom.app (op n)))) ∧
        IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
          (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2
          (cokernel (α.hom.app (op n))))) →
      ∃ (H : CoherentModules X) (a : G ⟶ H)
        (β : (completion X I).obj H ≅ F),
        (∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧
          IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
            (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (kernel a.hom)) ∧
          IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
            (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (cokernel a.hom))) ∧
        α = (completion X I).map a ≫ β.hom ∧
        ∀ (H' : CoherentModules X) (a' : G ⟶ H')
          (β' : (completion X I).obj H' ≅ F),
          (∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧
            IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
              (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (kernel a'.hom)) ∧
            IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
              (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (cokernel a'.hom))) →
          α = (completion X I).map a' ≫ β'.hom →
          ∃! γ : H ≅ H',
            a ≫ γ.hom = a' ∧
              (completion X I).map γ.hom ≫ β'.hom = β.hom)
